entries.claim: Plan 7 widened the trust-boundary trigger at SKILL.md:1095-1098 so it also fires when the design's data shows on a page outsiders can reach, but it left two older statements that still limit the trust question to outside input. README.md:53 says Seldon asks about trusting outside input "only when the design takes some", and SKILL.md:1119-1120 says "A design without one of these parts gets none of that part's questions", where one of the parts is outside input.
entries.failure_scenario: Take the spine-who-relies or spine-conventions seed: the repair-log PRD in samples/spine-conventions/prd.md (REPAIR-01..03, SHELF-01). Nobody outside the project sends anything in (the trust answer is "send nothing in through it"), but SHELF-01 changes shelf state on the catalog page that members browse from home. SKILL.md:1095-1098 says to ask the trust question here, and the spine-who-relies case's asks-trust.md grader requires it. SKILL.md:1119-1120 says a design with no outside input gets none of that part's questions, which forbids it. The README's spine paragraph also tells the user it's asked only when the design takes outside input, and the case list at README.md:117 says this case expects it. So the skill gives the model two opposite rules for this design. That is the same flip that failed full run 1 (spine-who-relies asking or not asking the trust question). The only evidence that the wider reading wins is one solo run per case after e46948c. The README states behavior that its own case list and graders contradict.
